question_text: What happens to a buck converter at exactly 100% and 0% duty cycle?
answer_text: At 100%, the high-side switch is always ON (V_out ≈ V_in). At 0%, the switch is always OFF (V_out = 0V).
explanation_text: At a 100% duty cycle, no switching occurs. The MOSFET acts as a continuous wire, the inductor saturates (acting as a wire with some DC resistance), and the input is passed directly to the output. At 0%, no energy is ever transferred, and the output capacitor fully discharges its remaining energy into the load.
bonus_question_text: What prevents many real-world buck converters from achieving exactly 100% duty cycle?
bonus_answer_text: The high-side N-channel MOSFET requires a "bootstrap" capacitor to drive its gate voltage higher than V_in. If the switch never turns OFF, the bootstrap capacitor can never recharge, causing the gate drive to fail.
